guidelines.detail: documentation rule FID-01 not applied (The description explicitly states that the employee collects money, while the reference includes a separate payment task and the generated model has no counterpart for it. No record indicates that payment was represented using a different BPMN element. FID-01 already requires modeling every distinct activity stated in the description.)

same as LRN-017 (The records show that explanatory or accompanying information was added to activity labels, although the description supports concise labels for the actions. LRN-017 already advises keeping associated details and outcomes out of activity labels.)

refines COL-07 (The description explicitly describes exchanges between the employee and chef, and the records show that the reference models the chef as a separate pool with message flows while the generated model uses a lane instead. This refines COL-07 by clarifying when internal roles are treated as independent communicating participants.)

documentation rule FLOW-01 not applied (The records show omitted sequence flows between described consecutive steps, including flows from start events and to end events. FLOW-01 already requires sequence flows to represent execution order, so this guideline is already covered.)

documentation rule FID-03 not applied (The label pairs show generated labels adding contextual wording beyond the shorter reference labels. The description confirms the underlying actions and events, so concise, faithful labels are supported. FID-03 already advises short, faithful labels, making this guideline already covered.)

refines COL-04 (The description confirms several participant-to-participant exchanges, while the records show missing message flows and one flow with its direction reversed. COL-04 already establishes sender-to-receiver direction and valid endpoints; this guideline applies that rule to exchanges explicitly stated in the description. The proposed guideline wording was not checked because no wording-check result wa)

documentation rule EVT-03 not applied (The description explicitly says the participant waits before continuing. The generated model represents that wait as a task, while the reference uses an intermediate catch event; EVT-03 already covers modeling a flow that waits for a trigger as a catch event.)

documentation rule FID-03 not applied (The label pairs show differences in how activities and events are named, and the description provides the actions and triggers those labels should reflect. FID-03 already advises short, faithful labels, so this guideline is already covered.)

documentation rule COL-04 not applied (The records show incorrect message-flow direction, missing flows, and generated flows with mismatched endpoints. COL-04 already requires message flows to run from sender to receiver and use valid interaction nodes, so this guideline is already documented. LRN-049 expresses a similar learned rule.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a participant collects or makes payment as a distinct step in a transaction

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an activity together with criteria, optional supporting actions, or a later outcome associated with it: Label the BPMN task with a concise verb-object phrase for the activity itself. Keep associated criteria, alternatives, and subsequent outcomes out of the label unless they define the activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity together with explanatory details or information communicated alongside it

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that distinct roles in an organization send information to one another about their work: model those roles as separate participant pools and represent each stated exchange with a message flow
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that distinct roles in an organization send information to one another about their work

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use bpmn:sequenceFlow for execution order between flow nodes in the same process or subprocess scope; set valid sourceRef and targetRef values.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states consecutive process steps, including steps immediately after a start event or before an end event

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity or event and includes contextual details that do not define the action itself

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that one participant sends information, a request, or an item to another participant.: Model the stated exchange as a message flow from the sending participant to the receiving participant, connecting appropriate interaction nodes in their respective pools and directing the flow from sender to receiver.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that one participant sends information, a request, or an item to another participant.

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description specifies that subsequent work begins only upon a condition or trigger occurring

rules_sent_back.instruction: Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that one participant communicates information, a request, a signal, or an item to another participant
